{{Short description|Rubber-tired automated people mover system manufactured by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2025}}
[[File:C810D Departing Fernvale.jpg|thumb|A [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Crystal Mover C810D|Crystal Mover (C810D)]] testing on the [[Sengkang LRT line]]]]
[[File:SIN Changi Airport Skytrain Set 17 & unknown @ Terminal 3 2023-10-14.jpg|thumb|[[Changi Airport Skytrain|Skytrain]] departing Terminal 3 station at [[Changi Airport|Singapore Changi Airport]]]]
The '''Crystal Mover''' is a rubber-tired [[automated people mover]] (APM) system for airport and [[urban rail transit]] applications manufactured at [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries]] (MHI) Mihara Machinery Works<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. Global Website {{!}} Mihara Machinery Works |url=https://www.mhi.com/company/location/miharaw |access-date=13 May 2023 |website=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. |language=en}}</ref> in [[Mihara, Hiroshima|Mihara, Hiroshima Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. The Crystal Mover, initially based on the Japanese APM standard, is used in [[automated guideway transit]] (AGT) systems in [[China]], [[Japan]], [[Singapore]], [[South Korea]], the [[United Arab Emirates]] and the [[United States]].

Since 2010s, MHI has been building and delivering a new family of AGT systems branded '''Urbanismo''' as the successor to the Crystal Mover. The Urbanismo family consists of a higher-speed model called "Urbanismo Super AGT" with a top speed of 120 km/h and three customizable models called "Urbanismo-22", "Urbanismo-18", and "Urbanismo-16" with a gross weight of over 22, 18, and 16 tonnes, respectively.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. Global Website {{!}} Transportation |url=https://www.mhi.com/products/engineering/transport.html |access-date=7 May 2023 |website=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. |language=en}}</ref>

== Urban rail systems ==
=== Japan ===
{{See also|List of urban rail systems in Japan}}
[[File:Yurikamome7500wiki.jpg|thumb|Yurikamome 7500 series EMU based on the Urbanismo-18 class (November 2018)]]
[[File:Newshuttle2021wiki.jpg|thumb|New Shuttle 2020 series EMU based on the Urbanismo-16 class (February 2016)]]
Between 2014 and 2016, Yurikamome, Inc., which operates the [[Yurikamome]] line in [[Tokyo]], purchased a fleet of 18 six-car 7300 series trainsets based on the Urbanismo-18 class<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=30 December 2019 |title=マカオに登場｢ゆりかもめの兄弟｣新交通の実力 |url=https://toyokeizai.net/articles/-/321598 |access-date=7 May 2023 |website=東洋経済オンライン |language=ja}}</ref> to replace all of the 18 six-car 7000 series trainsets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=三菱重工、ゆりかもめの新型108両を受注 |url=https://response.jp/article/2010/06/11/141480.html |access-date=7 May 2023 |website=レスポンス（Response.jp） |date=11 June 2010 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=三菱重工 {{!}} 新交通ゆりかもめ向け 全自動無人運転車両（AGT）48両を受注 |url=https://www.mhi.com/jp/news/1609235790.html |access-date=7 May 2023 |website=三菱重工 |date=23 September 2016 |language=ja}}</ref> Between June 2018 and June 2020, MHI also delivered 8 six-car 7500 series (upgraded version of 7300 series) trainsets to replace the fleet of 7200 series trainsets.<ref name="mhi20160923">{{cite web |date=23 September 2016 |title=新交通ゆりかもめ向け 全自動無人運転車両（AGT）48両を受注 2020年に向けて納入 |script-title= |trans-title=Order received for 48 AGT vehicles for Yurikamome to be delivered by 2020 |url=https://www.mhi.co.jp/news/story/1609235790.html |access-date=23 September 2016 |work=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries |publisher= |language=ja |location=Japan |archive-date=2 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180202015351/http://www.mhi.co.jp/news/story/1609235790.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Saitama New Urban Transit Co., Ltd., which operates the [[New Shuttle]] in [[Saitama Prefecture]], purchased a fleet of 5 six-car 2020 series trainsets based on the Urbanismo-16 class<ref name=":0" /> to replace the fleet of 3 six-car 1010 series trainsets and 2 six-car 1050 series trainsets from 2015 to 2020.<ref>[http://railf.jp/news/2016/06/28/160000.html ニューシャトル2020系23編成が営業運転を開始] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417124612/http://railf.jp/news/2016/06/28/160000.html |date=17 April 2019 }} - 鉄道ファン・railf.jp 鉄道ニュース、2016年6月28日</ref><ref>[https://railf.jp/news/2019/02/12/144500.html 三菱重工エンジニアリング,ニューシャトル2020系を追加納入] - 鉄道ファン 2019年2月12日掲載</ref><ref>[http://www.new-shuttle.jp/topics/2020/02/2020525.html 2020系　第5弾目の25（にいごう）編成がデビューします] - 埼玉新都市交通 2020年02月18日</ref> 

In [[Hiroshima]], [[Hiroshima Rapid Transit]] purchased 24 six-car 7000 series trainsets based on the Urbanismo class to replace the existing fleet of 23 six-car 6000 series trainsets and 1 six-car 1000 series trainset running on the [[Astram Line]]. The 7000 series entered service on 26 March 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=広島高速交通｜地下鉄車両ガイド｜日本地下鉄協会 |url=http://www.jametro.or.jp/guide/hiroshima.html |access-date=7 May 2023 |website=www.jametro.or.jp |archive-date=21 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231021094008/http://www.jametro.or.jp/guide/hiroshima.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

The [[Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation]] purchased a fleet of 12 five-car 330 series trainsets, which are similar in design to the Yurikamome 7300 series trainsets, to replace the fleet of 300 series trainsets running on the [[Nippori-Toneri Liner]] from fiscal 2022 to 2024.<ref name="ntl_press_20220623">{{Cite web |date=23 June 2022 |title=「日暮里・舎人ライナー」車両の更新を進めます～6月25日から運行開始～ |url=https://www.kotsu.metro.tokyo.jp/pickup_information/news/nippori_toneri/2022/ntl_p_2022062310510_h.html |accessdate=24 June 2022 |website=東京都交通局 |language=ja}}</ref><ref>[https://www.mhi.com/jp/news/story/200616.html 東京都交通局から日暮里・舎人ライナーの新型車両を12編成（60両）受注 三菱重工エンジニアリング、更新で混雑緩和等に貢献へ] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701164055/https://www.mhi.com/jp/news/story/200616.html |date=1 July 2020 }} 三菱重工業プレス・インフォメーション（2020年6月16日）2020年6月17日閲覧。</ref>

On 22 January 2025, MHI received an order from [[Seibu Railway]] for 3 four-car trainsets to replace the {{Ill|Seibu 8500 series|ja|西武8500系電車}}.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |date=22 January 2025 |title=8500系の後継として山口線（レオライナー）に新型車両を導入します |trans-title=New trains will be introduced on the Yamaguchi Line (Leo Liner) as successors to the 8500 series |url=https://www.seiburailway.jp/newsroom/news/20250122_8500keishinzou/ |access-date=2025-01-22 |website=Seibu Railway WEB |language=ja}}</ref><ref name=":12">{{Cite web |date=2025-01-22 |title=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. Global Website {{!}} MHI Receives Order for 3 New Series Trainsets (12 Cars) for Seibu Railway's Yamaguchi Line-- First Upgrade in 40 Years Will Boost Passenger Capacity and Convenience -- |url=https://www.mhi.com/news/250122.html |access-date=2025-01-24 |website=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd. |language=en}}</ref> Designated as the [[Seibu L00 series]], the first of these sets is expected to enter service on the [[Seibu Yamaguchi Line]] in March 2026, boosting capacity to carry passengers to two leisure facilities operated by the [[Seibu Group]]:  [[Belluna Dome]] and [[Seibuen Amusement Park|Seibu Amusement Park]]. <ref name=":12" /><ref>{{cite web |date=19 November 2025 |title=西武山口線，新形レオライナー「L00系」の第1編成が2026年3月にデビュー |trans-title=First train of new Seibu Yamaguchi Line Leoliner "L00 series" to debut in March 2026 |url=https://railf.jp/news/2025/11/19/001500.html |access-date=19 November 2025 |website=Japan Railfan Magazine Online |publisher=Koyusha Co., Ltd. |language=ja |location=Japan}}</ref>

=== Singapore ===
In Singapore, Crystal Movers operate on the [[Sengkang LRT line]] and the [[Punggol LRT line]], both managed by [[SBS Transit|SBS Transit Ltd]]. These cars have been operating since 2003 on the Sengkang LRT and on the Punggol LRT since its opening in 2005. There is a fleet of 41 cars of [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Crystal Mover C810|Mitsubishi Crystal Mover Contract 810]] in total for the two LRT lines.<ref name="c810a">{{cite news|title=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi Corporation Receive Order for Design, Manufacture, Installation and Commissioning of Singapore Light Rapid Transit Capacity Expansion – Vehicles and Electrical and Mechanical Systems for Sengkang and Punggol LRT Systems (C810A) |url=http://www.mhi.co.jp/en/m/news/story/1305221663.html|access-date=25 November 2015|date=22 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304052819/http://www.mhi.co.jp/en/m/news/story/1305221663.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.sgtrains.com/crystalmover.php | title=Mitsubishi Crystal Mover | work=SGTrains | access-date=28 September 2013 | archive-date=6 March 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150306023357/http://www.sgtrains.com/crystalmover.php | url-status=live }}</ref> An additional order was placed for 16 more cars under [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Crystal Mover C810A|Contract 810A]] with identical specifications to increase capacity on both LRT lines, with all trains delivered by 2016.<ref name="c810a" /> 

On 5 February 2021, the [[Land Transport Authority]] (LTA) announced that it has purchased 17 two-car [[Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Crystal Mover C810D|C810D]] trains for the Sengkang and Punggol LRT systems, which will replace the 25 existing one-car C810 trains.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sengkang-Punggol LRT to get 17 new two-car trains to boost capacity|url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/sengkang-punggol-lrt-17-new-two-car-trains-lta-depot-expand-14118006|website=CNA|date=5 February 2021|access-date=6 February 2021|archive-date=15 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515083925/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/sengkang-punggol-lrt-17-new-two-car-trains-lta-depot-expand-14118006|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2023, the LTA ordered an additional 8 C810D trains, which will replace the 8 existing two-car C810 trains.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-05-09 |title=8 new two-carriage trains to be added to Sengkang-Punggol LRT line |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/8-new-two-carriage-trains-to-be-added-to-sengkang-punggol-lrt-line |access-date=2025-10-02 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> This brings the total number of C810D trains ordered to 25, and the total fleet to 33 trains, comprised two-car C810A and C810D trainsets. The first C810D train arrived in Singapore on 23 November 2024 and entered passenger service on 15 July 2025,<ref name="8TSPLRT">{{cite news |date=19 Jul 2025 |title=New two-car trains begin service on Sengkang-Punggol LRT Line |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/sengkang-punggol-lrt-new-trains-third-generation-5238671 |access-date=15 July 2025 |work=CNA}}</ref> while the remaining 23 trainsets will arrive progressively and enter passenger service from Q3 2025 until the end of 2028.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-07-15 |title=Sengkang-Punggol LRT to get 15.8 per cent capacity boost with new trains |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/transport/sengkang-punggol-lrt-gets-15-8-per-cent-capacity-boost-with-new-trains |access-date=2025-10-02 |work=The Straits Times |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref> All trains will undergo testing and commissioning works before entering passenger service.

=== Macau ===
[[File:033B-033A Macau Light Rapid Transit Taipa Line(2) 11-12-2019.jpg|thumb|Urbanismo-22 vehicles operating on the Macau light rail system opened in 2019]]
On 31 December 2010, Macau placed a [[Macanese pataca|MOP]] 4.688 billion order for Urbanismo-22 vehicles nicknamed "Ocean Cruiser"<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> for the [[Macau Light Transit System]], which started commercial operation on 10 December 2019. It was free of charge until 31 January 2020.<ref>[http://www.macaudailytimes.com.mo/macau/20610-Mitsubishi-wins-LRT-tender.html Mitsubishi wins LRT tender] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110104061845/http://www.macaudailytimes.com.mo/macau/20610-Mitsubishi-wins-LRT-tender.html |date=4 January 2011 }}</ref>

== Specifications ==
[[File:Label in Crystal Mover.jpg|thumb|Logo of Crystal Mover]]

=== Original C810 ===

The specifications of an example configuration of the original Crystal Mover were given as:<ref name="mhi-techreview-jun2003">{{cite journal |url=https://www.mhi.com/technology/review/sites/g/files/jwhtju2326/files/tr/pdf/e403/e403182.pdf |title=New Product: Automated People Mover "Crystal Mover" Series |author=<!--Not stated--> |publisher=Mitsubishi Heavy Industries |journal=Technical Review |volume=40 |number=3 |department=Machinery Headquarters, Transportation Systems Department |date=June 2003 |lang=en |access-date=2025-09-06 }}</ref>

* Configuration: Single- or double-car
* Capacity (passengers): 105 (including 18 seats{{cn|date=September 2025}}) or 210 (including 36 seats)
* Vehicle mass: {{cvt|14.9|t}} per vehicle
* Vehicle dimensions (L × W × H): {{cvt|11.20|×|2.69|×|3.615|m|ftin}}
* Guide system: Side guide two-axis four-wheel steering system
* Electric system: Third rail at 750 volts [[direct current]]
* Gauge: {{track gauge|1850mm}}; guide rail span: {{cvt|3.2|m|ftin}}
* Maximum speed:
** Design: {{cvt|80|km/h|mph}}
** Operation: {{cvt|70|km/h|mph}}{{cn|date=September 2025}}
* Service acceleration and braking: {{cvt|1.0|m/s2|ft/s2 km/hs}}
* Emergency braking: {{cvt|1.3|m/s2|ft/s2 km/hs}}
* Car body structure: Aluminum alloy welded structure
* Traction motor: Two [[Three-phase electric power|3-phase]] alternating current [[induction motor]]s each with a continuous rating of {{cvt|80|kW|hp}}
* Propulsion control system: [[Insulated-gate bipolar transistor|IGBT]]–[[Variable-frequency drive|VVVF]] inverter vector control (individual control of each axis with variable load control)
* Brake system: [[Electronically controlled pneumatic brakes|Electric command pneumatic brake]] with [[regenerative brake]] (with stand-by brake, parking brake, variable load control and wheel slide prevention control)
